battery_overview: The Strategic Interpretation Battery is Call 7 — the client-facing strategy layer that sits above the three analytical batteries (Epistemic Motion, Forensic Analysis, Semantic Content). This is the Opposition View — the same instrument run with the defense's declared bias (Shell USA, Inc. and Shell Chemical, L.P.) rather than Judd's. The purpose is to understand how the same exchange looks from the other side of the table: what the defense would use, what they would fear, and how they would rank the analytical calls.
score_swap_note: Because these files were generated with Shell as the declared client, the model's internal scores are Shell-centric: client_value = Shell's gain, opposition_value = Jasso's gain. These scores are SWAPPED ON DISPLAY so that every SI document — prosecution and opposition alike — reads consistently: Client Value always means Jasso's gain, Opposition Value always means Shell's gain. Raw JSON: client_value = Shell · opposition_value = Jasso. Displayed: Client Value = Jasso · Opposition Value = Shell.

client_bias_declaration.note: This opposition run was biased with the defense's declared inputs. Shell is the client. The model was instructed not to fabricate findings. All use_this and watch_this items are drawn from battery output only — not from the original transcript.
client_bias_declaration.what_you_are_afraid_of: Credible testimony of defendant safety failures
client_bias_declaration.opposing_counsel_read: Use expert to establish defendant safety failures
client_bias_declaration.case_context: Cristoball Jasso v. Shell USA, Inc. and Shell Chemical, L.P. · Benjamin Gibson deposition, February 14 2025 · Direct examination by Ms. Kate Easterling for the Defense · Gibson serving as expert witness for Plaintiffs

pattern_field.label: Pair Strategic Signature
pattern_field.definition: A 2–3 word strategic label capturing what this pair means for the defense's case position. Generated from the defense bias, but displayed within Judd's normalized framework. Distinct from analytical battery pattern declarations — this labels strategic consequence from the opposing side's perspective.
pattern_field.scale: Qualitative (2–3 word phrase) · defense-perspective · strategic, not analytical
pattern_field.why_it_matters: Reveals the defense's strategic read on this exchange — what they see as the consequence of this pair for their case position.
pattern_field.examples: Credibility Risk, Narrative Anchor, Exposure Contained, Witness Deflection

fields.label: Summary
fields.definition: A 3–4 sentence strategic overview from the defense's declared perspective. Answers: what happened in this exchange that matters to Shell? What should their attorneys know before walking into or past this pair? The summary is direct and opinionated — a strategy brief from the opposing side, not a neutral description.
fields.why_it_matters: Shows Judd's team exactly how the defense reads this pair — what they think is useful, what they fear, and how they will frame their strategy.

fields.label: Pair Strategic Signature
fields.definition: A 2–3 word strategic label capturing what this pair means for the defense's case position. Generated from the defense bias. Displayed within Judd's normalized framework.
fields.scale: Qualitative (2–3 word phrase) · defense-perspective · strategic, not analytical
fields.why_it_matters: Names the defense's strategic consequence for this exchange — their read on what this pair means for Shell's position.

fields.label: Client Value (displayed — Jasso's gain)
fields.definition: DISPLAY VALUE ONLY. The raw JSON field opposition_value (Jasso's gain as seen from the defense model run) is displayed here as Client Value, normalized to Judd's perspective. Integer 0–10 assessing how useful this pair is for Jasso's side, as the defense model assessed it.
fields.scale: Integer 0–10. Raw JSON source: opposition_value. Display label: Client Value.
fields.why_it_matters: Shows how the defense model assessed Jasso's gain from this pair — a cross-check against the prosecution SI run's client_value.

fields.label: Opposition Value (displayed — Shell's gain)
fields.definition: DISPLAY VALUE ONLY. The raw JSON field client_value (Shell's gain as the declared client of the defense model run) is displayed here as Opposition Value, normalized to Judd's perspective. Integer 0–10 assessing how useful this pair is for Shell's side.
fields.scale: Integer 0–10. Raw JSON source: client_value. Display label: Opposition Value.
fields.why_it_matters: Shows how strongly the defense model rates this pair as useful for Shell — a direct read on the opposition's confidence in this exchange.

fields.label: Use This (defense perspective)
fields.definition: Battery findings the defense can actively use, ordered from most to least useful. Each item identifies: the utility level, which call produced it (1–6), which specific field contains it, and a 1–2 sentence explanation of the strategic value to the defense. Evidence drawn from battery output only.
fields.scale: Ordered array of {utility: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high', source_call: integer 1–6, source_field: field name, reason: text (1–2 sentences)}
fields.why_it_matters: Reveals the defense's playbook for this pair — what findings they will exploit and how, so Judd's team can anticipate and counter.

fields.label: Watch This (defense perspective)
fields.definition: Battery findings that represent risk or threat to the defense's side, ordered from highest to lowest threat. Each item includes a mitigation strategy the defense would employ. These are the defense's vulnerabilities — directly useful to Judd's team.
fields.scale: Ordered array of {threat_level: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high', source_call: integer 1–6, source_field: field name, mitigation: text (1–2 sentences)}
fields.why_it_matters: Surfaces the defense's own risk assessment — what they are afraid of in this pair and how they plan to mitigate it, which tells Judd's team exactly where to press.

fields.label: Call Rank (defense perspective)
fields.definition: All six calls from the source battery ranked 1–6 by strategic importance for this specific pair from the defense's perspective. Reveals which analytical dimensions the defense considers most valuable for their position on this pair.
fields.scale: Array of {call: integer 1–6, rank: integer 1–6, reason: text (1 sentence)} · all six calls · no ties
fields.why_it_matters: Shows the defense's analytical priority ranking — which calls they weight most heavily, revealing where their strategic focus lies on this pair.
